subject: Performance thresholds & load test playbook
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Performance thresholds & load test playbook

Sam —

Great to meet you (virtually) on Friday. Per our conversation here's the first-pass performance acceptance plan for the onboarding benchmark. Goal here is to align on measurable thresholds and test cadence so we can complete the onboarding milestone for the POC. High-level targets we propose:

- Latency (p95) <= 220 ms for typical prompts <= 256 tokens
- Sustained throughput: 120 req/s for 30 minutes (steady-state)
- Spike capacity: 350 req/s for 60s (burst handling)
- Error rate: < 0.5% (5xx / malformed) during tests

Proposed test approach:
- Staging run (non-prod) with representative traffic for 1 hour (phase A).
- Progressive ramp: 0 -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% load (each step 10 minutes).
- Two stress windows (phase B): 5x short bursts (60s) and a 20-minute sustained ramp to 2x expected peak.
- Observability: token-level latency, per-instance CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and end-to-end request traces.

Artifacts we'll share: load playbook (attached), k6 scripts, test config YAML, and recommended guardrails for RLS/quotas.

Proposed schedule: run staging test on Tue 2026-08-25 10:00 PT, followed by a 2-hour readout the same day. If that works we'll schedule a short production smoke the week after.

Attachments included: redwood_load_playbook_v1.pdf, test_config_acme.yml (see attached).

Next steps:
- Confirm the staging window (Sam)
- Confirm any constraints from your security or audit team around logs/data retention
- Ben and Sergio will share the k6 script and runbook with execution steps

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Eng <eng@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Performance thresholds & load test playbook

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the 8/25 slot:

- The latency target looks reasonable; can you confirm whether p99 is tracked as well and what you expect there?
- Our security team requires that test logs are retained for 90 days and that PII is redacted. Will Redwood provide request IDs and anonymized payload logs?
- For the spike runs, we'd like one of the bursts to include a heavier long-context prompt (approx 1,024 tokens) to validate KV cache behavior.

Assuming those are okay, 8/25 10:00 PT works. We also want a short pre-run sync (30 min) with our Eng team on 8/24 at 14:00 ET to walk through the k6 script and ensure our test agents are ready.

Sam Torres
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Health
sam.torres@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance thresholds & load test playbook (k6 script + execution notes)

Vanessa / Sergio —

Drafting the runbook now. Quick notes addressing Sam's questions:

- p99: We'll track p99 as an alerting metric. Expectation for p99 during steady-state is < 450 ms; during brief spikes p99 can increase but errors should remain < 1%. We'll log p99 in the report.
- Logs: Redwood will provide anonymized request traces and a per-request metadata CSV (request_id, timestamp, model_variant, latency_ms, status_code). No customer payloads will be stored beyond derived telemetry. Retention: we can retain telemetry logs for 90 days in your workspace; I will note this in the MAP.
- Long-context burst: k6 supports longer payloads; I'll attach the initial script. For the 1,024-token case we'll use the `long_payload.json` template in the repo.

Execution plan (short):
1) Pre-run: exchange staging API key (ephemeral), confirm IP allowlist, confirm agents (4 nodes)
2) Phase A: ramp test (0->100%), 10m steps
3) Phase B: 5 bursts at target spike, include one long-context burst
4) Cooldown & artifact collection: metrics export, GPU traces, traces sampling (5%)

I'll attach `k6_acme_script.js` and a minimal runbook. Can run the job from our infra or we can hand off scripts for your local execution.

Attaching: k6_acme_script.js

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Finalized MAP + pre-run sync link

Sam —

Thanks — I've incorporated Ben's notes and updated the mutual action plan. Summary of changes:
- p99 goal added (< 450 ms steady state).
- Telemetry retention set to 90 days and confirmed anonymization of payloads.
- Long-context burst added to Phase B; k6 script updated accordingly.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_acme.docx, redwood_load_playbook_v1.pdf, k6_acme_script.js, test_config_acme.yml

Pre-run checklist & links:
- Pre-run sync (30 min): Mon 2026-08-24 14:00 ET / 11:00 PT (Google Meet): https://meet.google.com/acme-pre-run
- Staging run window: Tue 2026-08-25 10:00 PT
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2026-RI-47

Ben / Sergio: please confirm who will own the readout and upload the artifacts into the shared Drive after the run. I created a Drive folder (link below) and the MAP points to the tests we will use for acceptance.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-for-acme-playbook

Thanks everyone — excited to get this validated.

Vanessa / Ben / Sergio —

All set from our side. Pre-run sync confirmed for 8/24 14:00 ET. Staging run on 8/25 10:00 PT is approved.

A few housekeeping points:
- We'll expect the anonymized telemetry CSV and the k6 raw output uploaded to the Drive folder within 4 hours post-run.
- Please include a short summary (1 page) with: achieved p95, p99, sustained throughput, peak throughput, error rate, and a short note on any anomalies.
- We reserve final acceptance until we complete the post-run readout and the MAP sign-off.

Thanks — we look forward to the readout.
